tasks.title: Persist and resolve controller on issue/update/resolve/list paths
tasks.description: In server/registry-service.js: issueApprovedDidRequest (line ~1275) passes controller: request.controller into upsertIssuedDidRecord (lines ~1373-1390). upsertIssuedDidRecord (line ~970) accepts input.controller, adding it to the insert branch (lines ~998-1039) and the update branch (lines ~1061-1091, `controller = $N`). syncWalletIssuedDid (line ~1435) accepts/passes controller: input.controller. syncWalletUpdatedDid (line ~1501) accepts input.controller and extends its `update did_records` statement (lines ~1503-1517) with `controller = coalesce($N, controller)` — MUST use coalesce, not a hard overwrite, so an update call that omits controller does not null out the existing persisted value. resolveDid (line ~1680) changes line 1698 from `controller: record.did` to `controller: record.controller || record.did` (ADR-002's fallback rule for the resolution endpoint, independent from task 4's). listRegistryDidRecords (line ~1637) adds `dr.controller,` to its explicit column SELECT list (lines ~1644-1664) — required for RegistryDidRow.controller to ever carry real data.
acceptance_criteria: issueApprovedDidRequest passes the request's persisted controller into upsertIssuedDidRecord, verified by a new test case in tests/registry-service-issue.test.ts

syncWalletUpdatedDid preserves the existing persisted controller when the update call omits controller (coalesce, not overwrite-to-null), verified by a new test case asserting the SQL uses coalesce($N, controller) and that a call without controller does not null the column

resolveDid returns controller = record.controller when present, and falls back to record.did when record.controller is null/undefined, verified by a new test case in tests/registry-service-issue.test.ts
listRegistryDidRecords' SELECT includes dr.controller, verified by asserting the query string/params in a new test case
npm test -- tests/registry-service-issue.test.ts passes

tasks.title: Cross-layer tests for full request-to-issue and update lifecycles
tasks.description: Add cross-function lifecycle tests exercising server/registry-service.js's exported functions together (following the mocked server/db.js query/withTransaction pattern already used in tests/registry-service-issue.test.ts and tests/registry-service-request.test.ts — this codebase has no real-Postgres test harness, so 'integration' here means multi-function flow through registry-service.js with a mocked DB layer, not a live database). Cover: (1) full request-then-issue cycle where controller ('C1') differs from subject_wallet_address, asserting the issued did_records row and resolveDid() both reflect C1; (2) update cycle where a DID with controller C1 is updated to C2 via syncWalletUpdatedDid, asserting a subsequent resolveDid() reflects C2 not C1; (3) legacy row simulation where controller is null on both did_requests and did_records rows, asserting buildDidDocumentForRequest falls back to subject_wallet_address (per task 4) and resolveDid() independently falls back to record.did (per task 5), per ADR-002's two non-unified fallback rules.
acceptance_criteria: A test asserts that a DID requested with controller C1 (≠ subject_wallet_address) and then issued via issueApprovedDidRequest results in a did_records row with controller = C1, and that resolveDid() for that DID returns controller = C1
A test asserts that updating an issued DID's controller from C1 to C2 via syncWalletUpdatedDid causes a subsequent resolveDid() to return controller = C2, not C1

A test simulates a legacy did_requests/did_records row pair with controller = null and asserts buildDidDocumentForRequest falls back to subject_wallet_address while resolveDid() independently falls back to record.did, confirming the two ADR-002 fallback rules do not interfere with each other
npm test -- tests/did-controller-lifecycle.test.ts passes

npx tsc --noEmit completes with no errors

tasks.notes: Completado por el orquestador tras interrupcion por limite de sesion del sdd-implementer. npx tsc --noEmit limpio. npm test -> 31 archivos, 273/273 passing. npm run build -> exit 0 (el classifier de Bash que bloqueaba build/lint ya se habia recuperado). npm run lint -> 0 errores, 1 warning pre-existente no relacionado (TokenGatingPanel.tsx, react-hooks/exhaustive-deps). Verificacion de wording (paso 5): re-grep de 'controller' en README.md y en RequestForm.tsx/IssuerPanel.tsx confirmo que todo texto de cara al usuario dice explicitamente 'does not grant authorization' o remite a la seccion README. Se detecto una ambiguedad menor no capturada por el sdd-implementer: README.md tiene dos conceptos distintos llamados 'controller' (el did_controller on-chain del contrato en la seccion Development, y el campo controller del DID Document JSON documentado por esta feature) sin cross-reference entre ambos. Se agrego una nota explicita de desambiguacion en la nueva seccion 'DID Document controller Field'. Re-verificado tsc/build/test limpios tras el cambio.
